mainTopic: Obeying the leader of your generation, and how בית דין sanctifies the new month
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא with more פסוקים showing that an appointed leader must be obeyed like the greatest leaders of the past, each in his own generation. The גמרא then returns to the משנה: רבי יהושע came to רבן גמליאל with his staff and money. רבן גמליאל kissed him and called him 'my teacher and my student,' and he praised a generation in which the great listen to the lesser. The second פרק ends here, and the third פרק, ראוהו בית דין, begins with a new משנה about cases where the court or three judges saw the new moon. The גמרא explains why each detail of the משנה is needed. It shows that sanctifying the month must be finished by day, because the פסוק calls it משפט. It also shows that one expert cannot sanctify the month alone, because even משה needed אהרן. Finally, the גמרא asks whether a witness can become a judge and begins a ברייתא about רבי עקיבא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A second verse puts weaker leaders next to the greatest ones
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds a פסוק from תהלים that places שמואל together with משה and אהרן. Since another פסוק places שמואל together with ירובעל, בדן and יפתח, the פסוקים are weighing those three as equal to the three greatest leaders.
steps.simpleTranslation: And another verse says: 'Moses and Aaron among His priests, and Samuel among those who call His name.' So the פסוק weighed three 'light' leaders as equal to three 'weighty' leaders.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings another פסוק to back up its point that every generation's leader counts as a real leader.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier פסוק listed ירובעל, בדן, יפתח and שמואל together. This פסוק lists שמואל together with משה and אהרן. Since שמואל appears in both lists, the two groups are being weighed against each other.

keyTerms.meaning: And it says: introduces another supporting פסוק
The verse weighed (treated as equal)
The 'light ones' of the world: less distinguished people
The 'weighty ones' of the world: the greatest people

phrases.english: And it says: "Moses and Aaron among His priests,
phrases.notes: תהלים 99:6

phrases.english: and Samuel among those who call His name."
The verse weighed three "light ones" of the world
phrases.notes: The 'light ones' are ירובעל, בדן and יפתח from the earlier פסוק. The 'weighty ones' are משה, אהרן and שמואל.

phrases.english: as equal to three "weighty ones" of the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous section, adding a second פסוק after the first one about ירובעל, בדן and יפתח.
steps.raayaObject: That a lesser leader in his generation has the same authority as a great leader
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 99:6, read together with the earlier פסוק that lists שמואל alongside ירובעל, בדן and יפתח

steps.title: Each leader in his own generation is like the greatest leaders
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא spells out the lesson. ירובעל is like משה, בדן is like אהרן, and יפתח is like שמואל, each in his own generation. Even the least distinguished person, once appointed leader, is like the greatest of the great.
steps.simpleTranslation: This tells you: Jerubaal in his generation is like Moses in his generation, Bedan in his generation is like Aaron in his generation, and Jephthah in his generation is like Samuel in his generation. This teaches that even the least of the least, once appointed leader over the community, is like the greatest of the great.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא states the practical lesson of the פסוקים: an appointed leader must be respected and obeyed like the greatest leaders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key words are 'in his generation.' The point is not that these people were personally as great as משה. Rather, the job of leader carries the same authority in every generation, so the people must listen to him.

keyTerms.meaning: In his generation
A leader appointed over the community
The mightiest of the mighty
The lightest of the light: the least distinguished person

steps.whatToRemember: An appointed leader's authority comes from the position. Even a less distinguished person who leads in his generation must be obeyed like משה in his.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not saying גדעון was as holy or wise as משה. It says that his authority over his generation was just as binding.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the reason רבי יהושע had to accept רבן גמליאל's decision about the date, even though he believed his own calculation.

phrases.english: To tell you:
Jerubaal in his generation is like Moses in his generation;
phrases.notes: ירובעל is another name for גדעון.

phrases.english: Bedan in his generation is like Aaron in his generation;
Jephthah in his generation is like Samuel in his generation.
To teach you that even the least of the least,
once he has been appointed leader over the community,
is like the greatest of the great.

steps.triggerLanguage: לוֹמַר לָךְ: יְרוּבַּעַל בְּדוֹרוֹ כְּמֹשֶׁה בְּדוֹרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the weighing described in step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Any person appointed as leader must be treated with the full authority of the greatest leaders.

steps.title: The judge 'in those days' means the judge of your own time
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes the פסוק 'and to the judge who shall be in those days.' Nobody could go to a judge who is not alive in his time, so the extra words must teach that you go only to the judge of your own days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it says: 'And you shall come to the priests, the Levites, and to the judge who shall be in those days.' Could you think a person would go to a judge who did not live in his days? Rather, it means you may only go to the judge of your own days.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a פסוק from דברים to show that the תורה tells us to follow the judge of our own generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'in those days' seem unnecessary, since obviously you can only go to a living judge. So they must teach something: accept the judge of your time, and do not wish for the greater judges of the past.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (asks why the words are needed)
The judge of one's own days
Judge

phrases.english: And it says: "And you shall come to the priests, the Levites,
phrases.notes: דברים 17:9

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶל הַשֹּׁפֵט אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם״,
phrases.english: and to the judge who shall be in those days."
But could it enter your mind
that a person would go to a judge
who was not in his days?
Rather, you have only to go
to the judge of your own days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third פסוק supporting the same lesson.
steps.raayaObject: That one must follow the judge of his own generation
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 17:9, read through the seemingly extra words 'in those days'

steps.title: Don't say the old days were better
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings a final פסוק from קהלת warning not to say that earlier times were better than now. You must accept the leaders of your own time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it says: 'Do not say: How was it that the former days were better than these?'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds one last פסוק that warns against wishing for the leaders of the past.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק attacks the attitude that today's leaders do not count because earlier ones were greater. It finishes the chain of proofs that the current leader must be obeyed.

keyTerms.meaning: The former days

steps.whatToRemember: Four sources show that each generation must follow its own appointed leaders: two פסוקים comparing leaders, the judge 'in those days,' and 'do not say the former days were better.'

phrases.english: And it says: "Do not say: How was it
phrases.notes: קהלת 7:10

phrases.english: that the former days were better than these?"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the final supporting פסוק to the chain.
steps.raayaObject: That one may not dismiss current leaders in favor of past ones

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבי יהושע takes his staff and money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה: רבי יהושע took his staff and money in his hand and went to רבן גמליאל on what was יום כפור by his own calculation.
steps.simpleTranslation: He took his staff and his money in his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes it to set up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying a staff and money is forbidden on יום כפור. By doing so on the day he believed was יום כפור, רבי יהושע showed that he fully accepted רבן גמליאל's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: His staff
His money

phrases.english: He took his staff and his money in his hand.
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the משנה. 'He' is רבי יהושע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ברייתא of proofs and returns to the משנה's story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע obeyed רבן גמליאל by traveling with staff and money on his own calculated יום כפור.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל stands, kisses רבי יהושע, and greets him
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that when רבן גמליאל saw רבי יהושע, he stood up from his chair, kissed him on the head, and greeted him as 'my teacher and my student.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: When he saw him, he rose from his chair, kissed him on his head, and said to him: Peace be upon you, my teacher and my student!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that describes how רבן גמליאל received רבי יהושע when he arrived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל had forced רבי יהושע to give in, but he now shows him great honor. The odd greeting 'my teacher and my student' is explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He kissed him
My teacher and my student

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
When he saw him,
phrases.notes: רבן גמליאל is the one who saw רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: he rose from his chair and kissed him on his head,
and said to him: Peace be upon you,
my teacher and my student!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's story with details from a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל honored רבי יהושע by standing and kissing him, calling him teacher and student.

steps.title: Why רבי יהושע is both teacher and student
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל explains his greeting. רבי יהושע is his teacher because he taught him Torah publicly, and his student because he obeyed רבן גמליאל's decree the way a student would.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'My teacher,' because you taught me Torah in public; 'my student,' because I issue a decree on you and you fulfill it like a student.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל explains the two titles he just used for רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two titles describe two different relationships. In Torah knowledge, רבי יהושע was the teacher. In authority, רבן גמליאל was the leader, and רבי יהושע obeyed him.

keyTerms.meaning: In public
Issues a decree
Fulfills it

phrases.english: "My teacher," because you taught me Torah in public;
"and my student," because I issue a decree upon you
and you fulfill it like a student.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the greeting from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teacher in Torah, student in obedience to the leader's decree.

steps.title: Fortunate is the generation where the great listen to the lesser
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל praises a generation in which great people listen to lesser ones. All the more so it is fortunate when lesser people listen to greater ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fortunate is the generation in which the great listen to the lesser; all the more so when the lesser listen to the great.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a closing line praising a generation in which people obey their appointed leaders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case of a great person listening to a lesser leader is the more impressive one, because it takes real humility. If that brings praise, then a generation where the lesser listen to the great certainly deserves praise, through a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: Fortunate is the generation
Listen to, obey
All the more so: an argument from a weaker case to a stronger one

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע's obedience to רבן גמליאל is the model: even a great scholar obeys the appointed leader, and such a generation is praised.

phrases.english: Fortunate is the generation
in which the great listen to the lesser;
all the more so when the lesser listen to the great.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story with a general lesson.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A generation in which people obey their leaders, especially when the great obey the lesser, is praiseworthy.

steps.title: How can obeying greater people be a קל וחומר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבן גמליאל's wording. Lesser people listening to greater people is not something we learn by קל וחומר. It is simply an obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: A קל וחומר?! It is an obligation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the end of רבן גמליאל's statement from Step 8. He made it sound as if lesser people listening to greater people is learned by a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר is used to learn something new from a weaker case. But lesser people obeying greater people is not new at all, because they must do it anyway. So calling it a קל וחומר seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument: if something is true in the weaker case, it is surely true in the stronger case
It is an obligation, something you must do anyway

phrases.english: A kal vachomer?!
phrases.notes: The גמרא is reacting to רבן גמליאל's last line in Step 8, about lesser people listening to greater ones.

phrases.english: It is an obligation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רבן גמליאל's concluding praise in Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל's claim that lesser people heeding greater ones follows by קל וחומר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר is not needed to teach something that is already required. Lesser people obeying greater people is a basic duty.

steps.title: The lesser people make the קל וחומר for themselves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reinterprets רבן גמליאל. When the lesser people see great people listening to them, they reason by קל וחומר that they must surely listen to the great people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: since the great people listen to the lesser people, the lesser people make a קל וחומר on their own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what רבן גמליאל really meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר is not the source of the obligation. It is the reasoning the lesser people use in their own minds. They see a great person like רבי יהושע give in, so they think, 'Surely we must give in too,' and they obey willingly.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces a corrected explanation
Greater people / lesser people
They apply a קל וחומר to themselves

steps.whatToRemember: Obeying the leaders of your generation is an obligation. When great people show humility, it inspires everyone else to obey as well.

phrases.english: Rather: since the great ones listen to the lesser ones,
the lesser ones apply a kal vachomer to themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of Step 9
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן גמליאל meant that the obligation itself comes from a קל וחומר
steps.terutzMaskana: The obligation exists anyway. The קל וחומר is the motivating reasoning the lesser people apply to themselves.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק אם אינן מכירין
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the second פרק of ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק 'אם אינן מכירין'.
steps.whatsHappening: The פרק is finished, and we say the traditional farewell to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying הדרן shows our wish to come back and learn this פרק again. A new פרק starts right after.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; the formula said when finishing a פרק
'If they do not recognize'; the opening words of this פרק, used as its name

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'If they do not recognize'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the story of רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: End of the second פרק of ראש השנה

steps.title: Moon seen by everyone, but not declared before night
steps.stepSummary: The new פרק opens. Suppose בית דין and all of ישראל saw the new moon and the witnesses were questioned. If בית דין did not manage to say 'מקודש' before nightfall, the month is מעובר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If בית דין and all ישראל saw it, and the witnesses were questioned, but they did not get to say 'מקודש' before it got dark, the month is made full (30 days).
steps.whatsHappening: The new משנה teaches that seeing the moon is not enough. בית דין must actually declare 'מקודש' on day 30, or the previous month gets 30 days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though everyone saw the moon and the witnesses were already checked, the declaration of בית דין is what makes ראש חודש. Without it, the 30th day passes as a regular day, and ראש חודש is the next day.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The court saw it'; the opening words and name of the new פרק
The witnesses were questioned and checked
'Sanctified!'; the declaration that makes the day ראש חודש
It got dark; nightfall
Made full; the previous month gets 30 days

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that seeing the moon makes the day ראש חודש. Only the declaration of בית דין does that, even when the whole nation saw the moon.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the Jewish calendar depends on the act of בית דין, not on the sky alone.

phrases.english: If the court and all Israel saw it,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the new moon.

phrases.english: and the witnesses were questioned,
but they did not manage to say 'Sanctified'
before it got dark, then it is made full.
phrases.notes: The month that is ending gets 30 days, so ראש חודש is the next day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק with a new משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without the declaration of בית דין before nightfall on day 30, the month is מעובר, even if everyone saw the moon.

steps.title: Only בית דין saw the moon
steps.stepSummary: If only בית דין saw the moon, two judges stand up and testify before the others, who then declare 'מקודש מקודש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If only בית דין saw it, two of them stand and testify in front of the others, and they say: 'מקודש, מקודש'.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case. The judges themselves saw the moon, but no outside witnesses did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is when the judges saw it at night, when the court cannot act on what it saw. Then seeing it themselves is not enough, and the normal order of testimony must still happen. Two judges act as witnesses, and the remaining judges act as the court and declare. Had they seen it by day, their own sight would be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Only; alone
They testify in front of them

phrases.english: If only the court saw it,
two should stand and testify before them,
phrases.notes: Two of the judges become witnesses in front of the other judges.

phrases.english: and they should say: 'Sanctified, sanctified.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second case to the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When only בית דין saw the moon, two judges testify before the others, who declare the month sanctified.

steps.title: Only three judges saw the moon
steps.stepSummary: Suppose only three judges saw the moon. Two of them seat two colleagues next to the third to form a new court, then testify before it. One judge alone cannot sanctify the month.
steps.simpleTranslation: If three saw it and they are a בית דין, two stand up and seat two of their colleagues next to the one remaining judge. Then they testify before them, and the court says 'מקודש, מקודש'. This is because one person alone is not trusted to do it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third case. Only three judges saw the moon, so if two become witnesses, just one judge is left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sanctifying the month needs a court of three. One judge is not enough. So the two witnesses bring in two other judges to sit with the remaining one, forming a new court of three to hear their testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: They seat some of their colleagues
The single one; the one judge left over
Authorized or trusted by himself alone

steps.whatToRemember: When the judges saw the moon at night, sanctifying the month needs two witnesses who testify before a court of three, so they must still set things up that way. Had they seen it by day, their own sight would be enough.

phrases.english: If three saw it and they are the court,
the two should stand and seat some of their colleagues
next to the single one,
phrases.notes: That's the third judge, who didn't stand up. Two others join him so there's a court of three again.

phrases.english: and testify before them, and they should say: 'Sanctified, sanctified,'

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין הַיָּחִיד נֶאֱמָן עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: because a single person is not authorized by himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third case, building on the procedure of Step 13
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A single judge cannot sanctify the month. A new court of three must be formed to hear the two judges' testimony.

steps.title: Why mention that the court and all Israel saw it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say that בית דין and all of ישראל saw the moon.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why does the משנה need to teach the case where בית דין and all of ישראל saw the new moon?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking why the משנה includes the detail that everyone saw the moon. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of the משנה is that if no one says 'מקודש' before nightfall, the month becomes מעובר. The extra detail that 'all of ישראל' saw the moon seems unneeded for that rule, so the גמרא asks what it adds.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Why do I need this? (asking why a detail is needed)
To teach / to state (in the משנה)
They saw it (the new moon)

phrases.english: Gemara: Why do I need it to teach
"the court and all Israel saw it"?
phrases.notes: This quotes the opening words of the new משנה from step 12.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה quoted in step 12
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the detail 'all of ישראל saw it' adds to the rule

steps.title: Even a widely seen moon still needs the declaration
steps.stepSummary: Without this detail, we might think that a moon everyone saw is public enough to skip the declaration. The משנה teaches that it is still מעובר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: since בית דין and all of ישראל saw it, it is already public, so they should not make the month full. The משנה teaches us that they do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra detail blocks a mistaken idea. Someone could think that public sighting alone is enough to start the new month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mistaken idea is that when everyone has seen the moon, the formal word 'מקודש' is not needed. The משנה teaches that even then, without the declaration before nightfall, the old month gets a thirtieth day and becomes מעובר.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed
You might have thought (introduces a mistaken idea)
It became public / well known
Let them make it full (add a thirtieth day)
It teaches us (that the idea is wrong)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the new month depends on the court's formal declaration, not just on everyone knowing the moon appeared.

phrases.english: It was necessary; it might enter your mind to say:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְרָאוּהוּ בֵּית דִּין וְכׇל יִשְׂרָאֵל —
phrases.english: since the court and all Israel saw it,
it has become publicly known,
so they should not make the month full;
phrases.notes: Making it full means the old month gets a thirtieth day, and the new month starts tomorrow.

phrases.english: it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The detail teaches that even a moon seen by everyone still needs the declaration before nightfall.

steps.title: Why mention questioning witnesses?
steps.stepSummary: If בית דין saw the moon themselves, why does the משנה mention that witnesses were questioned?
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the משנה taught that בית דין and all of ישראל saw it, why do I need 'the witnesses were questioned'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem in the wording of the משנה. If the judges saw the moon, witnesses seem unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses are needed to tell the court something it does not know. When the court saw the moon itself, questioning witnesses seems pointless, so the wording looks contradictory.

keyTerms.meaning: But since it taught
The witnesses were questioned

phrases.english: But since it taught
"the court and all Israel saw it,"
why do I need "the witnesses were questioned"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a second detail in the same line of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'נחקרו העדים' in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the court saw the moon, witnesses add nothing, so the phrase seems pointless.

steps.title: Reading it as a second case
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means 'or else': a separate case where witnesses were questioned but there was no time to declare.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: or else, if the witnesses were questioned and they did not manage to say 'מקודש' before nightfall, the month is מעובר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is listing two different cases, not one. The witness case is a separate case of its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Case one is when the court saw the moon itself. Case two is when witnesses came and were questioned. In both cases, if 'מקודש' was not said before dark, the month is מעובר.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means
Or else / alternatively
It became dark (nightfall)
Made full, so the old month has 30 days

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
or else, if the witnesses were questioned
and they did not manage to say "Sanctified"
before it became dark,
the month is made full.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה as two separate cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה describes one case with both a court sighting and witnesses.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists two cases: a court sighting, or else questioned witnesses.

steps.title: Why teach the witness case at all?
steps.stepSummary: Once the משנה taught that a missed declaration means מעובר, why add the witness case?
steps.simpleTranslation: But since it taught 'before nightfall, the month is מעובר', why do I need it to teach about questioning the witnesses at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further. Even as a separate case, the witness case seems to repeat a rule we already know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even a moon seen by everyone becomes מעובר without the declaration, then surely a moon reported by witnesses does too. So the second case seems to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: The questioning of the witnesses
At all

phrases.english: But since it taught
"before it became dark, it is made full,"
why do I need it to teach
the questioning of the witnesses at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן דִּתְנָא עַד שֶׁחָשֵׁיכָה הֲרֵי זֶה מְעוּבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The second case (questioned witnesses) as explained in step 18
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule of a missed declaration was already taught, so a second case seems repetitive.

steps.title: Not like money cases that finish at night
steps.stepSummary: Without the witness case, we might think the court could finish the sanctification at night, like דיני ממונות. The משנה teaches that it cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: questioning the witnesses is the start of the court case, and 'מקודש מקודש' is its end, so they could declare it at night. This would be just like money cases, as the משנה says: money cases are judged by day and may be finished at night. So here too they could sanctify at night. The משנה teaches us that they cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the witness case blocks a comparison to money cases. It shows that the sanctification cannot be finished after dark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In דיני ממונות, a case begun by day may end at night. One could compare: the witnesses were questioned by day (the start), so the declaration could come at night (the end). The משנה says no: once it is dark without 'מקודש', the month is מעובר.

keyTerms.meaning: The beginning of a court case
The end of a court case (the ruling)
Money cases
Just as it is with (a comparison)
At night

steps.whatToRemember: Every detail of the משנה has a purpose. 'All of ישראל saw it' teaches that a public sighting is not enough. The witness case teaches that sanctification is not like money cases: it cannot be finished at night.
steps.confusionAlert: The comparison to money cases is the mistaken idea (the סלקא דעתך), not the conclusion. The final rule is that they may NOT sanctify at night.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the rule that the declaration of the new month must happen during the day.

phrases.english: It was necessary; it might enter your mind to say:
let the questioning of witnesses be like the start of the court case,
and "Sanctified, sanctified" be like the end of the court case,
and let them sanctify it at night,
just as it is with money cases,
as we learned: money cases are judged by day
and may be finished at night.
So here too, they could sanctify at night;
it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: תֶּיהְוֵי חֲקִירַת עֵדִים כִּתְחִילַּת דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the case blocks a mistaken comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Questioning the witnesses starts the case, so the declaration could be finished at night, like דיני ממונות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sanctification may not be finished at night. Without a daytime declaration, the month is מעובר.

steps.title: Maybe the court really can finish at night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that קידוש החודש cannot be finished at night. Perhaps it really can, like דיני ממונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that it really is so, and the court may finish sanctifying the month at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on what it just said. Maybe the court really can finish קידוש החודש at night, just as in דיני ממונות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said the משנה teaches that the court cannot finish קידוש החודש at night. Now the גמרא asks why we should accept that. In money cases a trial that started by day may be finished at night, so maybe this works the same way. This sets up the need for a source.

keyTerms.meaning: But say it really is so
Money cases, which may be finished at night
The court's declaration of the new month

phrases.english: But say that it is indeed so?
phrases.notes: He means: maybe the court really can finish the sanctification at night, like in money cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption in step 20 that קידוש החודש cannot be finished at night.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that קידוש החודש may not be finished at night
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דיני ממונות may be finished at night, so why not קידוש החודש?

steps.title: The פסוק calls it משפט, so it must be by day
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק calls the month's declaration both חק and משפט. Just as a משפט is done by day, the final declaration must also be by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'For it is a statute for Israel, a judgment of the God of יעקב.' When does it become a 'statute'? At the end of the process. And the תורה calls that moment a 'judgment.' Just as judgment is by day, here too it must be by day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to prove that קידוש החודש must be finished during the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The month becomes a fixed 'חק' only when the court finishes its ruling. The פסוק calls that same final step 'משפט,' and judgment is done by day. So even the conclusion of קידוש החודש needs daytime, unlike the conclusion of a money case.

keyTerms.meaning: A statute, a fixed law
Judgment, a court ruling
The final ruling of a case

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the rule that the court must sanctify the month during the day. רבי זירא's answer in step 25 depends on it.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'For it is a statute for Israel,'
phrases.notes: תהלים 81:5

phrases.english: 'a judgment of the God of Yaakov.'
When does it become a 'statute'?
At the conclusion of the judgment,
and the Merciful One calls it 'judgment.'
Just as judgment is by day,
so too here, it must be by day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: ״כִּי חֹק לְיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מִשְׁפָּט לֵאלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21 with a פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קידוש החודש could be finished at night, like דיני ממונות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The final stage is called משפט, so it must be done by day.

steps.title: משנה: if the court saw the moon, two testify
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. If בית דין saw the new moon, two of them stand and testify before the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the court saw the moon, two should stand and testify before them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case of the משנה to set up a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the judges themselves saw the moon. Even so, the משנה says two of them must give formal testimony in front of the other judges.

keyTerms.meaning: The court itself saw the moon
And they testify before them

phrases.english: If the court saw it,
two should stand and testify before them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the court saw the moon, two of its members testify before the others.

steps.title: Why isn't seeing better than hearing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why testimony is needed. Hearing witnesses should not count for more than the judges' own seeing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? Hearing should not be greater than seeing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. If the judges saw the moon with their own eyes, why do they need to hear testimony?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a court relies on witnesses because it did not see the event itself. Here the judges did see it, which should be even stronger than hearing about it. So the testimony step looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Hearing should not be greater than seeing
And why?

phrases.english: And why?
Hearing should not be greater than seeing!
phrases.notes: Hearing means taking testimony from witnesses; seeing means the judges saw the moon themselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? לֹא תְּהֵא שְׁמִיעָה גְּדוֹלָה מֵרְאִיָּיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling just quoted in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's requirement that two judges testify
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The court's own seeing should be stronger than hearing witnesses, so testimony should not be needed.

steps.title: רבי זירא: they saw it at night
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that the משנה is talking about a case where the court saw the moon at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: For example, where they saw it at night.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the question by limiting the משנה to a case where the judges saw the moon at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 showed that the court can only act by day. When the judges saw the moon at night, they could not act on what they saw. So the next day they must hear it as formal testimony, like any other report.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, in a case where
At night

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
For example, where they saw it at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: כְּגוֹן שֶׁרָאוּהוּ בַּלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The court saw the moon in a way it could act on, so testimony seems pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: They saw it at night, when the court cannot act, so by day they need testimony.
steps.whatToRemember: A court that saw the moon itself still needs testimony when it saw the moon at night, because the court only acts by day.

steps.title: משנה: three judges saw it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case. If three judges saw the moon, two testify, and two colleagues sit with the remaining judge to form a court.
steps.simpleTranslation: If three saw it and they are a court, two should stand and seat two of their colleagues next to the single one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another case from the משנה to set up a question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here only three judges saw the moon. Two of them become witnesses, so the third alone is left. Other judges join him so there is again a full court of three to hear the testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: And they seat some of their colleagues
The single one, the judge left alone

phrases.english: If three saw it, and they are a court,
two should stand and seat some of their colleagues
next to the single one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When three judges saw the moon, two testify, and colleagues join the third to form a court.

steps.title: The same question on the three judges
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question here. Why isn't the judges' own seeing better than hearing?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? Here too, let us say: hearing should not be greater than seeing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats its earlier question on this new case of the three judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These three judges saw the moon themselves. So, just as before, there seems to be no need for testimony and for adding colleagues.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too, let us say

phrases.english: Why? Here too, let us say:
Hearing should not be greater than seeing!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? הָכָא נָמֵי נֵימָא: לֹא תְּהֵא שְׁמִיעָה גְּדוֹלָה מֵרְאִיָּיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the question of step 24 to the case of step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The requirement of testimony and added judges in the three-judge case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The judges saw it themselves, which should be better than hearing testimony.

steps.title: The night answer would just repeat the earlier case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the night answer here. If this case is also about seeing at night, it is the same as the earlier case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that here too it is where they saw it at night, then this is the same as that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the obvious answer before anyone can give it. If this case is also about night, why would the משנה teach it twice?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's night answer worked for the earlier case. If it is used again here, the three-judge case adds nothing new, and the משנה does not repeat itself for no reason. So the question still stands, and the answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say
This is the same as that

steps.confusionAlert: The night answer is not being called wrong. The point is only that it can't be the reason for this case, because then the משנה would be repeating itself.

phrases.english: And if you say here too
it is where they saw it at night,
this is the same as that!
phrases.notes: "That" is the earlier case of the court seeing the moon, which רבי זירא explained as night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the question of step 27 by ruling out רבי זירא's answer from step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the night answer for the three-judge case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both cases are about night, the second case teaches nothing new.

steps.title: The second case teaches that one judge cannot act alone
steps.stepSummary: The second case is needed for its ending. It teaches that a single judge cannot be מקדש the month alone, even though an expert may judge money cases alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ending of the case is what the משנה really needed to teach: one person alone is not trusted to act by himself. You might have thought this: we learned that money cases need three judges, but a publicly recognized expert may judge even alone. So here too, one expert could be מקדש the month alone. The משנה teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 28. The second case is not a repeat of the first, because it teaches something new in its ending.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is not about seeing the moon. It is about the one judge who is left over. He cannot be מקדש the month alone, even if he is an expert, so two colleagues must join him. This is different from דיני ממונות, where a recognized expert may judge by himself.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter part or ending of a statement or משנה
It would have entered your mind to say (a mistaken first thought)
Money cases
An expert recognized by the public
It comes to teach us

phrases.english: The latter part is what it needed
phrases.notes: This means the end of the case: the one judge who is left needs two colleagues to sit with him.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאֵין הַיָּחִיד נֶאֱמָן עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: that an individual is not trusted by himself.
For it would have entered your mind to say:
since we learned that money cases are judged by three,
and if he was an expert recognized by the public
he may judge even alone,
so here too, let him sanctify the month alone
it teaches us that this is not so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28 by finding a new teaching in the second case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shifts the purpose of the clause: the case is needed for its ending, not its beginning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Like money cases, a recognized expert could be מקדש the month alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: קידוש החודש needs a full court. One judge alone cannot do it, even if he is an expert.

steps.title: Why not let an expert act alone here too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: why not say that here too an expert may be מקדש the month alone?
steps.simpleTranslation: But why not say that here too an expert may act alone?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 29. It asks why קידוש החודש should be different from money cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 said we might have compared קידוש החודש to money cases, and the משנה teaches that we may not. The גמרא now asks what is wrong with that comparison. It wants a reason why an expert's power to judge alone does not reach the sanctifying of the month.

keyTerms.meaning: But let us say
Here too

phrases.english: But let us say that here too an expert may act alone?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule that step 29 found in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that an expert cannot be מקדש the month alone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an expert may judge money cases alone, the same logic should allow him to be מקדש the month alone.

steps.title: Even משה רבינו needed אהרן with him
steps.stepSummary: No expert was ever greater than משה רבינו, yet הקדוש ברוך הוא told him to be מקדש the month only together with אהרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no expert in Israel greater than משה רבינו. Yet הקדוש ברוך הוא told him that he could not do this until אהרן was with him. As it is written: "And ה׳ spoke to משה and to אהרן in the land of Egypt, saying: This month shall be for you."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a פסוק. Even the greatest expert of all could not be מקדש the month alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The command about the month was said to both משה and אהרן. So even משה, the greatest expert ever, needed a partner. If he could not do it alone, no single expert can.

keyTerms.meaning: משה our teacher
With you
As it is written
This month shall be for you, the command to sanctify the months

steps.whatToRemember: קידוש החודש can never be done by one person alone, even by the greatest expert. Even משה needed אהרן.

phrases.english: There is no publicly recognized expert in Israel
greater than Moshe our teacher,
and the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him:
not until Aharon is with you,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיֹּאמֶר ה׳ אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְאֶל אַהֲרֹן
phrases.english: as it is written: "And ה׳ spoke to Moshe and to Aharon
in the land of Egypt, saying:
This month shall be for you."
phrases.notes: שמות 12:1–2. The word "you" here is plural, speaking to both of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לְךָ מוּמְחֶה לְרַבִּים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹתֵר מִמֹּשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 30 with a פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a פסוק that sets קידוש החודש apart from money cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An expert could be מקדש the month alone, as in money cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even משה needed אהרן, so no single person can be מקדש the month.

steps.title: Can a witness also be a judge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the משנה means that someone who saw the event can also judge it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this to say that a witness can become a judge?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the משנה, and this line sets up the next move. In the משנה, a judge who saw the moon himself still sits on the court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of three judges who saw the moon, the third judge was also an eyewitness. Yet he joins two colleagues to judge the case. So the משנה seems to hold that a witness may become a judge, and the next step will check this against another opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say? (drawing a conclusion to test it)
A witness becomes a judge

phrases.english: Is this to say that a witness becomes a judge?
phrases.notes: The third judge in the משנה saw the moon himself, and he still sits on the court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the question of a single judge to a new question raised by the same case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the משנה hold that someone who saw an event can also judge it?

steps.title: Perhaps the משנה goes against רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה may not follow רבי עקיבא, and it begins quoting a ברייתא about a סנהדרין that saw a killing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that our משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא? For it was taught in a ברייתא: a סנהדרין that saw someone kill a person...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that the משנה conflicts with רבי עקיבא. It starts quoting a ברייתא as its source, and the quote continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה lets a witness be a judge, it may disagree with רבי עקיבא. The ברייתא about judges who saw a murder will show his view. This would leave the משנה against an important תנא, which the גמרא prefers to avoid.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion the גמרא will test)
The high court of judges
Killed a person

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not finished here. רבי עקיבא's actual opinion comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Shall we say that our Mishnah is not in line with Rabbi Akiva,
for it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: סַנְהֶדְרִין שֶׁרָאוּ אֶחָד שֶׁהָרַג אֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ —
phrases.english: A Sanhedrin that saw someone kill a person —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 32 by testing its conclusion against רבי עקיבא's view in a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's apparent rule that a witness can become a judge
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about a סנהדרין that saw a killing seems to show that רבי עקיבא does not allow a witness to judge, so the משנה would go against him.
